newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

A threat of deportation is looming large over about 100,000 illegal Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia as an extended deadline of amensty offered by the Malaysian government expired at midnight last night.
The government is continuing efforts through Bangladesh missions abroad for extradition of all those accused named in the chargesheet of the Bangabandhu (Sheikh Mujibur Rahman) murder case.

Over 200,000 Bangladeshi workers, who were staying illegally in Malaysia, have legalised their stay taking the opportunity provided by Malaysian government during August-December 1996 -- they obtained temporary work permit. But another 200,000 Bangladeshi workers failed to avail themselves of this opportunity.
Agriculture Minister Matia Chowdhury has asked fertiliser dealers to sell urea at the fixed price or face cancellation of dealership at three days' notice.
Two trade missions, one from Thailand and the other from Australia, are likely to visit Bangladesh by March and April this year.
The World Bank has removed two out of eight projects from its "problem and risk category" following tangible progress in recent times.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria has said he assessed the overall economic activities with an optimistic note and that there are no "unusual macroeconomic strains."
Bangladesh received more water in the first 10-day cycle of January than in sharing formula of the water treaty with India, but far less in the last two cycles of the month, reports UNB news agency.
